title: Why to even bother with commercial indie game development, if some kid without any serious gamedev knowledge can beat me with AI anyways, which it 100x faster, cheaper, and most importantly, better?
author: ImpressiveFocus303
selftext: As it says in the title.

comments.author: Hisagi10
comments.body: short answer,  not every game is good, you need to be good developer and make good game to sell

comments.author: Low-Efficiency-9756
comments.body: this has always been the case sans ai.

comments.author: shimroot
comments.body: Coding is not the issue. Building a good game (or any product for that matter) is hard regardless if coding is done with AI or not

comments.author: Iggnitious
comments.body:
Because ideas are implemented differently - AI can't build the game that you want to build because only you can build the game you have in your head. 

AI is a tool, but if the implementation and the ideas suck, the game will suck. Likewise, coding it yourself is the implementation, but if your idea sucks, you're no better off - only that the AI developer can get it 95% done much quicker.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: I mean, you have AI too. So either your contribution or the kids contribution will result in a more meaningful product. And the ability to slog through 10,000 lines of code to find a persistent bug is no longer a factor, instead pushing the meaningful skill disparity into your ideas, communication and overall game/design sense. It only becomes an "unfair" playing field if one person refuses to use the tools available.

comments.author: EnthiumZ
comments.body: Decent quality game is hard to make. It involves novel ideas, creative art that catches the eye and most importantly it's usually something new which AI might have trouble with. Keep in mind, commercial indie game development is already extremely difficult long before AI becomes a factor. We have indie devs making excellent games without any AI with some even good ideas and they hardly make any money. AI is not gonna be any help here either with one shots. You can use it to make certain parts of your game but actual direction needs to come from a human others project is dead from the start in a sea of their dead slop games, AI made or otherwise.

replies.author: Capital-Hedgehog-278
replies.body: I'm 100% agree on this. I'm tired of seeing ai would overcome people with great talent. People have the most stupidity and brilliant ideas ever.

replies.author: Capital-Hedgehog-278
replies.body: Plus most of the ai post we see is noise, instead of thinking too much on it and worrying, we should focus on our games.

comments.author: West-Contribution797
comments.body:
Games are like art. 
Fine pieces can be done by 1 man in the basement and sold quite well.
Some art are made for profit and it work quite well.
Meanwhile ai art exist in niche category of cheap labour where it replaces artists for shitty ads or concepts.

comments.author: ArtArtArt123456
comments.body:
now imagine being that kid. imagine him typing, word for word, your post into reddit. ...what do you think that means? that nobody should make anything?

no. it just means it is a very competitive field. 

also why would that kid make everything 100x faster cheaper and better? unless you deliberately don't want to use AI?

comments.author: Capital-Hedgehog-278
comments.body:
We will only have a decade to build our fortune as true indie game developers. So let’s move fast, take risks, and bring our greatest ideas and creativity into this world.

I’m not an AI game developer but I’m not against using AI either. I believe the tools we use shouldn’t define our creativity, the ideas, passion, and vision we bring to life.

comments.author: mallcopsarebastards
comments.body:
This is like an author giving up once the type writer was invented, because some kid could write a book faster than he could. 

Getting the words on paper isn't the hard or interesting part, just like writing the code isn't the hard or interesting part. Abstracting yourself away from that work doesn't have to hurt you.

A good game design team will always make a better game than some random kid who doesn't care about what he's making, just like some kid who cares deeply about what he's making will always make a better game than a game design team that are just trying to mass produce bullshit. 

The tools don't make the game, they just accelerate the process.

comments.author: ponderdiggums
comments.body:
Do you enjoy making games? Cars can get somewhere faster than I can, but I still enjoy a nice walk. 

Making games is hard, even harder to make a good one - in the future, doing so without AI will be viewed as an achievement. I have no doubt many will choose to express their artform this way. 

Have you worked on games in the past? AI or not, game dev familiarity goes a long way.

comments.author: Alaaaah
comments.body: That's right you better give up.

comments.author: Fruitsy
comments.body: Making the game itself is rarely the biggest hurdle imo. Its marketing and honestly a lot of luck. The barrier to entry for making games will be lower than ever but that just means there will be thousands of look-alikes out there. Like there are so many card game rogue-likes or Vampire Surivor Clones out there but only a small handful ever gain traction.  There will always be a market for novel ideas, regardless of AI involvement.

comments.author: Tiendil
comments.body:
1. He can not.
2. If he can, then you know less than that kid.
